title: Autotune prober + synthetic rolling eval for FlashAttention v2/v3 kernel selection
creator: Aisha Khatri
description: Build a synthetic workload-driven prober and rolling evaluation harness to surface correctness and performance regressions when selecting between FlashAttention v2 and v3 kernels at runtime. The goal is to create a lightweight, deterministic probe that runs alongside the runtime, exercises representative prefill and decode patterns (short/long contexts, many small requests, batched streaming), and produces telemetry used by the kernel selector autotuner to (1) detect regressions early, (2) widen the coverage of kernel compatibility tests, and (3) enable safe staged rollouts with quantifiable ramp metrics.
acceptance_criteria: Synthetic prober binary integrated into runtime test image and enabled by default on canary tier
Prober generates a compact telemetry vector (p50/p95 latency, mem high-water, kernel switch count, correctness hash) available to our telemetry pipeline
Rolling-eval dashboard with automated regression alerting when p95 latency increases >5% or mem HWM increases >10% vs baseline
Autotuner uses prober output to tag kernel candidates as PASS/DEGRADED/FAIL and backs off to safe fallback when needed
plan: Design synthetic workload shapes (prefill_long, prefill_short, burst_small_requests, streaming_decode_jitter) — 1 day
Implement prober harness that can run deterministically with a seed and record per-kernel metrics — 3 days
Wire prober telemetry into metrics pipeline (Prometheus + routed trace + compact JSON blob to s3 for replay) — 1 day
Create rolling-eval pipeline that compares nightly prober runs to baseline and surfaces regression alerts — 1 day
End-to-end tests and canary rollout to runtime-canary for 2 weeks — 2 days to schedule/dev + monitoring
progress_updates: 2025-01-15: Created ticket and sketched prober design in runtime doc. Initial workload shapes enumerated (short/long prefill, decode burst, streaming token jitter).

2025-01-20: Prober prototype committed to branch feature/eng/attn-prober. Implemented prefill_short and prefill_long workloads and deterministic RNG seed. Unit tests added for correctness hash. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1427

2025-01-24: Telemetry schema finalized with Observability team: compact vector = [kernel_name, seq_len, p50_ms, p95_ms, mem_hwm_mb, kernel_switches, correctness_hash]. Added end-to-end export to telemetry staging bucket.

2025-01-28: Discovered a regression: FlashAttn-v3 path shows higher mem HWM for 32k prefill shape on A100-80GB in synthetic runs. Reproduced locally; created investigation subtask ENG-623410. Plan: add memory fence and workspace sizing clamp in v3 shim as mitigation.

2025-02-02: Rolling-eval prototype dashboard online (Grafana) with nightly comparisons. First alert threshold tuned to p95 >5% and mem HWM >10%. Preparing canary rollout notes and PR for config flags.
decisions: Use deterministic synthetic workloads (seeded RNG) to make nightly comparisons reliable rather than fully randomized traces
Send compact telemetry blobs to minimize cardinality and avoid trace flooding; keep full debug traces gated behind flag
Autotuner will operate on discretized PASS/DEGRADED/FAIL labels derived from the prober vector rather than raw continuous scores for safer rollouts
Fallback policy: if a kernel candidate is labeled FAIL on the canary tier, do not promote to production; if DEGRADED, enable canary-only routing with traffic cap 5%
tradeoffs: Deterministic synthetic workloads increase reproducibility but may miss real-world corner cases — will complement with sampled production trace replays later
Compact telemetry reduces metrics costs but loses some signal granularity — full traces kept behind an opt-in debug flag to preserve investigability
Conservative autotuner labeling reduces rollout speed but lowers risk of customer-visible regressions
testing_plan: Unit tests validate correctness hash for a corpus of token sequences across v2 and v3 kernels
Integration test runs prober in containerized runtime image across matrix of shapes (seq 128, 512, 2048, 8192, 32768) and records metrics
Long-running soak: schedule nightly prober for 14 days on canary pool with alerting enabled
Replay harness: ability to re-run synthetic jobs against historical model/checkpoint and kernel builds stored in s3 for bisecting regressions
rollout_plan: Merge prober to main branch behind feature flag runtime.attn_prober.enabled=false by default
Enable on canary tier (runtime-canary) for 2 weeks; monitor rolling-eval dashboard
If stable, flip feature flag to enabled for limited dedicated clusters (low-traffic customers) for 1 week
Full prod enable only after 2 weeks of green canary + dedicated checks and no unresolved FAILs
rollback_conditions: Any night where p95 latency regresses >10% on canary compared to baseline => immediate demote of new kernel and revert config
Memory HWM increase >15% or any OOM during prober runs => rollback and create high-priority incident
Correctness hash mismatch between kernels for same inputs => immediate fail and block promotion
notes: Coordinate with Observability to avoid high-cardinality labels when adding kernel metadata
We should add a follow-up to instrument quantized kernel paths separately because workspace usage differs significantly
Consider adding a small corpus of customer-supplied prompts behind an opt-in flag to catch real-world regressions
